The method replaces the usual numerical integration through the compressor with approximate analytical integration.
The overall compressor performance is found as a perturbation of the design performance in terms of linear and quadratic expansions in the deviation from design flow rate and speed.
The amount of numerical work in finding the coefficients of the quadratic expansions is not negligible.
The method is expected to provide reasonably accurate results for speeds varying up to 10% from design and flow rates varying up to 4% from the design flow.
The single stage performance is represented using dimensionless work coefficient (Y), pressure coefficient (Ψ), and adiabatic efficiency (η) as functions of the flow coefficient (φ).
The compressor is assumed to be made up of an infinite number of infinitesimal stages, allowing the temperature to be considered a continuous variable along the compressor axis.
The adiabatic efficiency is defined as the ratio of the isentropic temperature rise to the actual temperature rise per stage.
The flow coefficient is defined as φ = mRT/(pUA), where m is mass flow rate, R is the gas constant, T is temperature, p is pressure, U is rotor speed, and A is flow annulus area.
The area distribution of the compressor is fixed by the design geometry and can be determined from the flow coefficient distribution.
The temperature ratio, pressure ratio, and adiabatic efficiency of the overall compressor are expressed as quadratic equations in terms of the deviation from design flow rate and speed.
